answer: Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Each submission hangs on the signal of a task receipt, and the ridge is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The ivory of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, clawed back after a replayed submission, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain.
